Multiplayer

Build a game with Kit

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Run the smallest gameDeclare the writersAdd a shared interactionMove fast state to authority when neededGrow the game

Kit starts from registered game entities. Their fields declare which machine writes each value and how it is synchronized. Commands express a player action that the authority can accept or reject. Use this path when the game's natural authoring unit is a Godot script entity.

Run the smallest game#

From the repository root, enter the development shell and build Hello Net:

Shell
nix develop
bash build/build_scripts.sh examples/hello_net
"$GODOT" --path examples/hello_net

Choose Host. In a second terminal with the same environment, launch another copy and choose Join. Arrow keys move the local player's square.

Shell
HELLO_LATENCY=120 "$GODOT" --path examples/hello_net

The delay makes the two presentation clocks visible: local movement responds immediately, while a remote square is interpolated from buffered observations.

Declare the writers#

The Hello Net player has owner-streamed coordinates and an authority-written seat:

Odin
x, y: f32 `gd:"owner,wire=f16"`,
pid:  u8  `gd:"replicate"`,

Untagged fields remain local. The scene factory and network registry track entity identity, creation, ownership, and removal. Follow the Kit quickstart for the complete entity declaration, session setup, frame pump, and teardown.

Add a shared interaction#

Write a command that validates and mutates its target. Local prediction can run that target mutation before the host's verdict. Keep cross-entity consequences in the authority command hook: a chest command removes loot from the chest; the accepted consequence credits the player's inventory.

The command guide explains submission, rejection, and the target-local mutation rule. Start with a range check and one item before adding an inventory, quest reward, or ownership transfer.

Move fast state to authority when needed#

Hello Sim runs the square through Kit's simulation lane. Predicted fields use gd:"predict,interp"; a pure @(gd_tick) procedure advances them from typed input. The authority runs the same tick and supplies corrections.

Work through the simulation quickstart, then select the network profile that matches invited co-op, a listen server, or a trusted dedicated process. For contested objects, use the timeline guide to choose prediction and presentation.

Grow the game#

Cavecrawl combines interactions, inventory, AI, progression, and recovery. The Kit package overview maps those systems to their imports. Keep the smallest example's frame and shutdown lifecycle working as new systems are added.
